sourceAudit.note: Source facts were reconciled against current main. The linked remediation ledger preserves historical checks and qualification evidence; implementation changes are not device or binary qualification.

statusDefinitions.implemented: The code path is present in this branch. It does not imply a passing test, native build, device exercise, or public release.
statusDefinitions.partial: The core path is present, while a material capability, performance measurement, integration, or qualification remains open.
statusDefinitions.gated: The capability intentionally stays disabled or experimental until its stated external or platform evidence exists.

localization.qualityStatus: Structural locale coverage is present: 5,459 messages across 37 locales and 47,662 explicitly allowlisted English-fallback entries. Metronome and legacy-import strings use assistant-generated drafts without independent/native-speaker review; five legacy-link converter labels remain explicit English fallback. Native-speaker fluency review is not established by key counts or generated-file checks.

productBoundaries.open: The bounded mixed-media deck, profile-local Saved picks/history, exact filters, mood/familiarity filtering, explicit local taste controls, per-pick hide/restore/reset, capped isolated OPDS samples, exact-public-ID adaptation matching, two-to-three-item comparison, private co-present shortlist voting, and opt-in encrypted Saved-pick sync are implemented. Optional AI reranking uses opaque IDs and bounded metadata with deterministic fallback. Open Library adds browse-only catalog records; when the existing OverDrive gate is enabled, connected borrower catalogs can add local-only candidates that are revalidated by exact library and book IDs before opening. OverDrive remains disabled by default and availability is checked only in its existing detail flow. Feature acceptance, provider exercises, native builds and physical-device qualification have not run for this slice. No research-cohort feature is in scope.
Comic reader and import code are integrated on main. Reader interoperability and device qualification remain open; an old conflicted PR is not a current integration blocker.

Venue controls now provide a one-touch host pause that persists the held session and stops local and paired-phone app capture without resuming microphones. It does not control external mixers. OS/MDM kiosk hardening and room reservations require platform configuration or a real scheduling provider and remain unavailable; singers/history remain profile-scoped, and device qualification is open.

Steam receiver/cloud/family/internet/controller/capture sources and RomM exact-copy/browser/stream/native/save workflows are integrated. Native RomM requires isolation ABI 1: desktop and Android adapters are verified, and the webOS/Tizen descriptor-only worker passed x64/ARM64 containment and ARMv7 compilation. The iOS 26 Enhanced Security worker and packaging source are implemented, with simulator extension linkage/packaging verified and signed-device acceptance still open. tvOS lacks the required supported containment API and native cores remain disabled. Actual cores, native SDK app builds, deployed optional services and real account/network/device acceptance remain open.

The in-app workspace, detached desktop video and shared-engine non-video windows are implemented on macOS, Windows and Linux. Pane semantics expose focus activation, and interactive game panes request their FocusNode so the game-input lease transfers with pane focus. Profile-scoped recovery checkpoints support explicit resume through existing library/source/reader owners after restart; they never deserialize credentials or launch games automatically. Local recovery/profile/source/catalog and player-startup regressions pass. Native builds, concurrent decoder limits, audio/input ownership, crash injection, native screen-reader acceptance and physical-device qualification remain open.

ABI v2 native host/process helpers and runtime/source/notice packaging hooks are integrated for desktop, Android, Apple and TV routes. The canonical sample-only catalog is published with GitHub OIDC/Sigstore identity and verified client-side, with rollback and expiry enforcement. Empty Ed25519 keys keep schema-v1 envelopes closed; the separate upstream MilkRust Ed25519 root remains unprovisioned. Ordered PCM artifacts are promoted in the app lock, but their receipts mark native execution unqualified. Beyond the exact Linux x64 package UI-path qualification recorded in IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, runtime/app qualification across release targets, driver/render fidelity, broader licensed catalog assets and physical-device qualification remain open.

productBoundaries.area: Shared music playback and persistent queues
productBoundaries.open: Shared playback and 10,000-track durable queue behavior are implemented with bounded pages, leased scratch indexes and occurrence identity. Multi-index edits retain rollback leases; tail appends keep the incremental path. This change passes formatting and focused static analysis; no tests/builds/CI were run. Existing P06/P07 regressions are recorded in music STATUS. Physical offline cold start, live provider and receiver/vehicle qualification remain open.

productBoundaries.area: Neural motion smoothing and NPU providers
productBoundaries.open: The persisted Playback → Motion smoothing preference defaults to Off; Neural is opt-in. Source and package configuration include Android LiteRT model packs by default and pinned Performance/Balanced/Quality ONNX graphs plus native PME/runtime packaging hooks for Windows and Linux. At runtime, the service resolves provider availability against the active stream and renderer, reports provider/model/power/thermal state, and falls back to MPV smoothing where supported or Off. NPU availability still depends on matching hardware, drivers/providers and optional vendor SDK or compiled-context inputs; bundled model files and provider adapters do not prove accelerator access. Recorded evidence covers model/runtime packaging, Android APK model checks, and local Linux GPU inference with null video/audio output. Apple package builds, exact current-release package qualification, provider execution across device/OS combinations, visible frame quality, presentation pacing and A/V sync remain open. Proprietary SDK access and compatible hardware remain external prerequisites.

Implemented DV/FEL routing is automatic by default in ordinary builds, with persisted explicit Off/manual controls and compatibility fallback, under the 2026-11-09 owner directive. Experiments remain accurately identified as experimental. Reference-output, signaling, seek/sync and platform evidence remain required; packaging alone is not image-quality qualification.
Keep OverDrive disabled until provider approval, deployed gateway controls, assigned sandbox credentials, and live fulfillment qualification are available.

Compatible public GitHub-hosted runners are the default. Private ephemeral JIT is used for private resources or platform constraints. Existing builds validate their own revisions, not subsequent remediation commits.

findings.title: Profile source loading and adapter ownership
findings.qualification: Profile data is staged and published as one owner-scoped snapshot; stale loads and adapter callbacks are generation-guarded. The delayed A→B→A completion-order regression passes. Credential-refresh acceptance remains unqualified.

findings.title: Exact-commit required-job release gate
findings.qualification: Normal releases capture one main build workflow and independently verify every required reusable-CI child from the same source and run attempt before creating the stable tag. Legacy standalone checks and recovery load the required-job contract from the exact CI source SHA. The changed workflow has not yet passed exact-SHA CI on the default hybrid route; negative-gate and successful-candidate evidence remain pending.

findings.title: Verified Apple purchase entitlement
findings.qualification: A StoreKit purchase event cannot grant a new entitlement until verified transaction history confirms ownership; empty history is treated as unknown, revocation is handled separately, and history responses cannot overwrite a newer purchase-stream event. StoreKit configuration and sandbox replay, restore, invalid, refund, and offline cases remain unqualified.

findings.title: Profile-bound, bounded settings backup and restore
findings.qualification: The initiating profile identity and mutation generation are captured before storage awaits; both WebDAV directions require an active profile and abort owner-bound requests, outbound JSON is encoded into a 4 MiB-capped buffer, restore is streamed with the same cap, and import checks ownership through guarded writes and rollback. Deterministic tests cover an in-flight profile switch, oversized outbound rejection before sending, malformed remote JSON, redirect and timeout handling; settings-import tests cover malformed entries and rollback after a write failure. Live WebDAV server and device-lifecycle qualification remain open.

findings.title: Source edit option preservation
findings.qualification: Edits retain unrecognized provider options and carry the applicable NFS, OAuth drive, and sync identity fields. Provider-by-provider edit/reconnect round-trip acceptance remains pending.

findings.title: Independent encrypted and provider sync targets
findings.qualification: Cloud and provider targets retain independent acknowledgments, failure reporting, and retry state. Two-device conflict convergence against live provider accounts remains unqualified.

findings.title: Atomic bounded discovery Undo history
findings.qualification: History appends then keeps the newest 500 actions within an atomic database read-modify-write. Focused tests cover the 500-history and 240-seen bounds, concurrent database updates, and failed/retried Undo at the 250-pick cap. Optional Saved-pick sync now has deterministic two-device coverage for an offline device applying a removal after rejoining; this does not establish all conflict or live-provider flows, or device and power-loss qualification. Undo and review history remain profile-local and are not replicated.

findings.title: Complete-scan index deletion reconciliation
findings.qualification: A generation mark is reconciled only when a scan completes; focused tests cover stale-entry pruning, cancellation, and superseded scans preserving cached rows until the current scan finishes. Device-level interrupted-scan durability remains unqualified.

findings.title: Bounded source index and page retrieval
findings.qualification: UI retrieval is SQL-paged. Merged server-library scans mark visited copies by generation in SQL and reconcile stale copies with a single database delete; their only per-scan external-ID cache retains at most 128 shows. Local directory snapshots remain bounded in memory and on disk. Target-device latency, memory, and I/O budgets have not been measured.

findings.title: Reusable NFS RPC sessions and bounded read-ahead
findings.qualification: Adapters reuse a bounded RPC session pool and permit at most four read-ahead lanes. NAS interoperability, cancellation, and repeated throughput measurements remain unqualified.

findings.title: Durable bounded publication download jobs
findings.qualification: The app persists jobs, applies per-profile quota and free-space bounds, recovers interrupted transfers, and limits native background transfer to explicit safe subsets. Active readers hold an exact-edition lease that blocks its removal. Crash/resume, low-space, and platform lifecycle acceptance remains open.

findings.title: Cross-device shared book identity
findings.qualification: Explicit shared-library and shared-item IDs can map provider entries and uniquely compatible editions. Copied local books are not automatically joined by title or content digest; households must establish matching IDs on participating devices.

findings.title: Sync failure isolation, capacity, and recovery
findings.qualification: Per-target retry, bounded state, causal annotation tombstones, compaction, and encrypted recovery exist. A deterministic three-device test verifies a stale offline device applies a deletion tombstone and converges after rejoining. No remote device roster or retirement/revocation operation exists; generation pruning is local to the syncing device. Live-provider behavior remains unqualified.

findings.title: Reader browser and native platform qualification
findings.qualification: On 2026-11-13, the pinned Playwright 1.62.1 reader suite passed locally on kspld0 with system Chromium: five comic-layout checks and three Flutter EPUB/comic/Arabic browser flows. This local run does not qualify the hosted workflow. Android WebView, Apple WebKit, Windows WebView2, Linux external-browser lifecycle, and physical reader acceptance remain separate.

findings.title: Capability, release, and documentation truth
findings.qualification: The capability ledger and repository guard cover the current findings, privacy disclosure, and release facts. GitHub lists v3.0.33 as the latest published release (source commit 240994590dd3e5411ee3b02c2bcfc0a1fd51a431); its recorded platform coverage is complete. Structural localization totals are summarized in the canonical coverage report and checked against this manifest; native-speaker fluency review is still not established. See docs/maintainers/releases/v3.0.33.json and docs/localization/coverage.json.

findings.title: Automatic metadata lookup privacy expectations
findings.qualification: Metadata lookup defaults off. The privacy notice identifies the title/year/episode/NFO identifier sent to Trakt when opted in and states that file bytes, full paths, and source credentials are excluded. A deterministic request-capture test verifies the cleaned filename query, year, and selected catalog ID while checking private paths and canary values are absent. Live Trakt-account acceptance remains open.

findings.title: MilkDrop visualizer and preset pack workflow
findings.qualification: The pinned source implements the documented legacy .milk/.milk2 profile and verified pack workflow; see SOURCE_COMPLETION.md and IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md. The 2026-11-11 local x64 Linux MilkRust build and GL/GLES smoke checks rendered 12 changing frames for both bundled samples. An exact Linux x64 package's first-use visualizer UI path was exercised on a VM, but this does not qualify native PCM tap execution or other targets. The app lock records ordered PCM ABI 1 and all four required tap exports for Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows; mpv-build package manifests still mark native execution unqualified. The local Arch host lacks libmujs.so.3, liblua5.2.so.0 and libdisplay-info.so.1. Reference fidelity/corpus conformance, cross-platform runtime qualification, separate upstream MilkRust Ed25519-root custody, physical-device qualification, and broader community-pack rights remain open; the canonical sample-only keyless catalog is published, and .milk2 is implemented in source.
